_readme: Wording for the ABC tracker. Items with a status only appear on the live site when status is published; pending and draft items show on preview builds so you can read them in place. Interface labels (questions, buttons) have no status and are always shown.

labels.heading: Log a moment
labels.early: Did you notice anything before it got big?
labels.lookedLikePlaceholder: What did you see or hear?
labels.exactMinutes: minutes, if you want to be exact

labelNudge.text: Words like this mean different things to different people. A few words about what it looked like ("dropped to the floor and cried for 5 minutes") make your notes more useful.

safetyCard.title: Safety comes first
safetyCard.body: Moments like this can be frightening. If anyone is hurt or in danger, call 911. When things are calm, it's worth telling your child's doctor or BCBA what happened.
safetyCard.talkLine: Talk to your child's doctor or BCBA.

lines: What happened right before a moment is often the most useful part of a note.
A week of notes can show patterns, like time of day, that are hard to see in the moment.
Describing what you saw ("cried and dropped to the floor") tells your child's team more than a label does.
You can export your notes as a PDF to bring to a doctor, BCBA or teacher.
Your notes stay on this device. No one else can see them unless you export them.
Notes about easier days help too: they show what was different.

walkthrough.title: How this works, in 30 seconds
steps: Say you asked your child to put their shoes on, and they dropped to the floor crying.
Tap what they did: crying, dropping to the floor.
Tap what happened right before (asked to put shoes on) and right after (you waited, then helped). Both are optional.
Save. After a few moments are logged, "What you're noticing" shows the patterns in what you recorded.

whatNext.title: Saved. What happens next
items: Export once a week. The PDF is one page per week with counts at the end.
Bring it to your BCBA. The tracker records; it never interprets.
Keep going on hard days and easy ones; patterns need both.

insights.tooFew: Log a few more moments and patterns will show up here.
insights.countNote: Counts of what you recorded. They don't say why anything happened.

questionsToBring.heading: Questions you could bring to a BCBA, your pediatrician, or your child's teacher
questionsToBring.before: Most moments came right after this: “{label}”. What could help at those times?
questionsToBring.after: Afterwards, “{label}” was recorded most often. Is that worth talking through?
questionsToBring.time: Most moments happened between {from} and {to}. What usually happens around then?
questionsToBring.early: “{label}” often came first. What could we do when we notice it?
